summary: Verification of piecewise gradient easing fix in useScrollGradient (App.js line 93: `const t = rawT <= 0.6 ? rawT : 0.6 + Math.pow((rawT - 0.6) / 0.4, 1.4) * 0.4;`). Re-measured computed background-color of [data-testid=app-root] and heading contrast at the same 11 sections tested in iteration_45. RESULT: PASS — all 11 sections have contrast >= 3.5:1 against their white headings. The HIGH-priority regressions from iteration_45 (Industries 1.33, BusinessReality 1.55, WhySpecializedIT 2.56) and the MEDIUM regression (Compliance 3.91) are FULLY RESOLVED. Late-third descent (rawT 0.6->1.0) still darkens smoothly and continuously through rgb(22,56,95) -> rgb(2,8,18) without abrupt plateau.

computed_gradient_data.note: Section rawT values are slightly HIGHER than iteration_45 baseline because DOM had slight layout differences (ebook popup CSS, viewport, etc.), but position within gradient is what matters and all headings now sit on sufficiently dark backgrounds.
computed_gradient_data.descent_pacing_assessment: First 60% (rawT 0-0.6) is EXACTLY the original linear gradient stops as intended (0.1->rgb(192,212,232) matches stops[1], 0.2->rgb(150,182,212) matches stops[2], ..., 0.6->rgb(22,56,95) matches stops[6]). Final 40% is eased so the interpolation SLOWS down: at rawT=0.7 the color is rgb(17,47,82) instead of stops[7] rgb(14,40,72) — subtle but keeps the descent visually gradual rather than dropping straight to near-black. At rawT=1.0 it still reaches the final rgb(2,8,18) darkest stop. Descent is smooth and continuous through all 5 sampled points (0.65,0.75,0.85,0.95,1.0).

critical_code_review_comments: Piecewise easing curve is well-chosen — keeps linear behavior in the critical 0-60% zone where content-dense white-text sections live, and only applies gentle ease to the trailing 40% where sections already have huge contrast margin (7+:1).

Ebook popup (EbookPopup) auto-opens on scroll and covers ~35% of viewport; not related to this test but persistently blocks visual verification of section contrasts in screenshots. Consider requiring explicit user trigger or delaying to onExitIntent only.
useScrollGradient still reads document.body.scrollHeight on every scroll frame — fine for perf but consider throttling via rAF if perf becomes a concern on low-end devices (also noted iteration_45).
scroll-behavior:smooth on html can interfere with programmatic scrollTo in tests; tests can override, but if this hurts SPA anchor UX consider scoping to specific anchor links only.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — all 11 target sections pass AA large contrast against their white headings; late-third descent visually smooth

context_for_next_testing_agent: Gradient regression from iteration_45 is FULLY RESOLVED by piecewise formula on App.js:93. All 11 downstream bg-transparent sections (Industries, BusinessReality, WhySpecializedIT, Compliance, HowItWorks, CaseStudy, Credentials, ProudPartners, CyberGame, RiskReversal, FAQSection) now have contrast 3.52 to 17.64 — well above WCAG AA large threshold (3.0). Even-spaced scroll stops match the raw gradientStops array 1:1 for rawT<=0.6 and reach the darkest stop rgb(2,8,18) at rawT=1.0. If future changes touch the easing formula or gradientStops, re-run the same measurement approach (scroll each of the 11 sections to top-of-viewport, read [data-testid=app-root] backgroundColor, compute contrast vs the section's h2 color). Ebook popup auto-opens on scroll — dismiss it or ignore for gradient measurements (it doesn't affect app-root bg color).
rca of the issue: N/A — iteration_45 issue is resolved. Root cause of the iter_45 regression was Math.pow(rawT,1.6) globally, which flattened the color-lookup domain in the first ~60% and left middle sections with white text on light-blue bg. Current piecewise fix preserves linear behavior exactly where the white-text sections live (rawT 0.3-0.6) and only eases the trailing dark zone.
